title: Impact of IPO Lockup Expiry on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology. This is appropriate because we have a specific event (lockup expiry) occurring at event_day = 0 for each stock, and we want to measure abnormal returns around this date. The key assumption is that in the absence of the lockup expiry, stock returns would follow their normal relationship with market returns (captured by the market model using beta). Any deviation from expected returns around the event can be attributed to the lockup expiry.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s57_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns using market model
# AR = R_it - (alpha + beta * R_mt)
# We'll estimate alpha from pre-event period and use provided beta

# First, let's examine the data structure
cat("Data dimensions:", dim(data), "\n")
cat("Event day range:", min(data$event_day), "to", max(data$event_day), "\n")
cat("Number of stocks:", length(unique(data$stock_id)), "\n")

# Define event windows
estimation_window <- data$event_day >= -250 & data$event_day <= -51
event_window <- data$event_day >= -10 & data$event_day <= 10

# Calculate abnormal returns for each stock
calculate_abnormal_returns <- function(stock_data) {
  # Estimate alpha using estimation window (if available, otherwise use full pre-event)
  est_data <- stock_data[stock_data$event_day < 0, ]
  
  if(nrow(est_data) > 5) {
    # Estimate alpha from pre-event period
    model <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = est_data)
    alpha <- coef(model)[1]
    beta_est <- coef(model)[2]
  } else {
    # Fallback: use provided beta and assume alpha = 0
    alpha <- 0
    beta_est <- unique(stock_data$beta)[1]
  }
  
  # Calculate abnormal returns
  stock_data$abnormal_ret <- stock_data$ret - (alpha + beta_est * stock_data$mkt_ret)
  return(stock_data)
}

# Apply to each stock
data <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do(calculate_abnormal_returns(.)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Calculate daily average abnormal returns across all stocks
daily_aar <- data %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    aar = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_stocks = n(),
    se_aar = sd(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n_stocks),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR)
event_window_data <- daily_aar[daily_aar$event_day >= -10 & daily_aar$event_day <= 10, ]

# CAR for different windows
car_day0 <- sum(event_window_data$aar[event_window_data$event_day == 0])
car_minus1_plus1 <- sum(event_window_data$aar[event_window_data$event_day >= -1 & event_window_data$event_day <= 1])
car_minus5_plus5 <- sum(event_window_data$aar[event_window_data$event_day >= -5 & event_window_data$event_day <= 5])
car_full_window <- sum(event_window_data$aar)

# Statistical significance tests
# Standard error for CAR
se_car_day0 <- sqrt(sum(event_window_data$se_aar[event_window_data$event_day == 0]^2))
se_car_minus1_plus1 <- sqrt(sum(event_window_data$se_aar[event_window_data$event_day >= -1 & event_window_data$event_day <= 1]^2))
se_car_minus5_plus5 <- sqrt(sum(event_window_data$se_aar[event_window_data$event_day >= -5 & event_window_data$event_day <= 5]^2))

# T-statistics
t_stat_day0 <- car_day0 / se_car_day0
t_stat_minus1_plus1 <- car_minus1_plus1 / se_car_minus1_plus1
t_stat_minus5_plus5 <- car_minus5_plus5 / se_car_minus5_plus5

# Print main results
cat("\n=== IPO LOCKUP EXPIRY EVENT STUDY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("\nCumulative Abnormal Returns (CAR):\n")
cat("CAR(0): ", round(car_day0 * 100, 3), "% (t-stat: ", round(t_stat_day0, 3), ")\n")
cat("CAR(-1,+1): ", round(car_minus1_plus1 * 100, 3), "% (t-stat: ", round(t_stat_minus1_plus1, 3), ")\n")
cat("CAR(-5,+5): ", round(car_minus5_plus5 * 100, 3), "% (t-stat: ", round(t_stat_minus5_plus5, 3), ")\n")
cat("CAR(-10,+10): ", round(car_full_window * 100, 3), "%\n")

# Statistical significance
cat("\nStatistical Significance (p < 0.05):\n")
cat("CAR(0): ", ifelse(abs(t_stat_day0) > 1.96, "Significant", "Not significant"), "\n")
cat("CAR(-1,+1): ", ifelse(abs(t_stat_minus1_plus1) > 1.96, "Significant", "Not significant"), "\n")
cat("CAR(-5,+5): ", ifelse(abs(t_stat_minus5_plus5) > 1.96, "Significant", "Not significant"), "\n")

# Robustness check: Cross-sectional test
cross_sectional_cars <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_individual = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop')

t_test_result <- t.test(cross_sectional_cars$car_individual, mu = 0)

cat("\nRobustness Check - Cross-sectional t-test for CAR(-1,+1):\n")
cat("Mean CAR: ", round(mean(cross_sectional_cars$car_individual) * 100, 3), "%\n")
cat("t-statistic: ", round(t_test_result$statistic, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value: ", round(t_test_result$p.value, 4), "\n")

# Additional robustness: Sign test
positive_cars <- sum(cross_sectional_cars$car_individual > 0)
negative_cars <- sum(cross_sectional_cars$car_individual < 0)
total_cars <- length(cross_sectional_cars$car_individual)

cat("\nSign Test:\n")
cat("Positive CARs: ", positive_cars, " (", round(positive_cars/total_cars*100, 1), "%)\n")
cat("Negative CARs: ", negative_cars, " (", round(negative_cars/total_cars*100, 1), "%)\n")

# Plot the results
plot_data <- event_window_data
plot_data$car_cumulative <- cumsum(plot_data$aar)

print(ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = event_day)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y = aar * 100), stat = "identity", alpha = 0.7, fill = "lightblue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = car_cumulative * 100), color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Average Abnormal Returns and Cumulative AR around Lockup Expiry",
       x = "Event Day (0 = Lockup Expiry)",
       y = "Return (%)") +
  theme_minimal())
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect to find negative abnormal returns around the lockup expiry date, with the most significant impact on day 0 or shortly after. The magnitude should be approximately -2% to -5% for CAR(-1,+1), as the release of previously restricted shares typically increases supply and puts downward pressure on stock prices. The effect should be most pronounced immediately around the expiry date, with some potential anticipation effects in the days leading up to the event. The cross-sectional analysis should show that a majority of stocks (>60%) experience negative abnormal returns during the event window.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare CAR before and after lockup expiry.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The lockup expiry leads to a negative impact on CAR.
